metadata.title: Apple Stock Defies AI Selloff: Is It the Market's Safe Haven?

content.text:
Apple (AAPL) stock has gained 30.61% in 2026 while Nvidia (NVDA) has lost 21.35%, according to TradingView data. The AI selloff has left the market rewarding the company that spent least on AI infrastructure.
Apple's climb has not been without its volatility. Shares slid 7.5% between Oct. 23 and Nov. 3, which suggests holders swapped AI spending risk for valuation risk. However, the tech giant has showed remarkable resilience in a market currently under pressure.
Why Did Apple Stock Avoid the AI Selloff?
Apple cut capex by 29% in fiscal 2026, CFO Dive reported. Research and development spending still rose 32% to $45.8 billion.
Peers moved the other way. Amazon plans $220 billion in capex this year and Microsoft $170 billion. Alphabet targets up to $205 billion and Meta $145 billion.
Investors long criticised Apple as an AI laggard. The same lean spending now works as insulation, since peers carry the data center bills.
Apple instead rebuilt Siri on Google's Gemini models through a June partnership. Apple still buys from the boom, however. It runs heavier AI tasks on Nvidia chips inside its Private Cloud Compute servers, CFO Dive added.
Is Apple's Resilience Earnings or Rotation?
Earnings explain part of it. Apple reported September-quarter revenue of $114.5 billion, up 12% from a year earlier.
Apple Chief Financial Officer Kevan Parekh guided to 7% to 10% growth for the holiday quarter. He said AI gives customers a reason to upgrade, which ties the new Siri to iPhone demand. He also flagged rising memory costs.
Rotation explains the rest. The Nasdaq 100 sat about 15% below its October record as of Nov. 18. Apple set an intraday record of $360.83 on Nov. 13.
Only Apple and Amazon were beating the S&P 500 fund SPY's 7.4% gain as of Nov. 17. Apple's 5.31% one-day jump on Nov. 4 was its best session in 1.5 years. The stock then slipped only 1.5% while the Nasdaq fell 5.52%.
Nvidia's slide has company-specific causes too. Shares fell 11.3% in premarket trading after Jensen Huang's resignation on Nov. 12.
A 30% rebound on his return faded within a day. The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has also reportedly opened a probe into Nvidia's accounting practices. TradingView shows Nvidia down 33.01% over three months, which leaves Apple as the cleaner exposure to the same theme.
What Could End Apple's Safe-Haven Run?
The same analysis put Apple at about 39 times earnings against 28 for Microsoft. That premium assumes the holiday guidance holds.
The case also depends on AI spending staying unrewarded. Analyst estimates put peer capex above $700 billion this year. If that spending starts producing revenue, the old criticism of Apple as an AI laggard could return.
